name: Burn
label: Revelation
lede: Four songs on one Revelation seven-inch in 1990, with a swing and a stop-start menace nobody in New York hardcore had heard, and then twenty-seven years until the full-length.

eras.title: Four songs, fire and fusion
eras.text: By 1989 the youth crew sound had hardened into a formula. Gavin Van Vlack, out of Side by Side and Absolution, wanted a band that swung, and he found a singer in Chaka Malik who could ride it. One seven-inch later, New York hardcore had a new way to move.

years.p: Van Vlack recruits singer [[Chaka Malik|072518f3-a3d6-40af-8d5a-9f30d25de77e]], drummer [[Alan Cage|65d4abbb-054b-4106-a826-0cb2b306341e]] of Beyond and bassist Alex Napack of [[Pressure Release|d129edff-83d0-4d95-976c-87b6a2dd57fd]], who names the band.
years.xp: Drummer John Krisciun played with Burn before Cage.

q: It was so lawless, that you could really do anything.
years.src: No Echo (Gavin Van Vlack interview) · The Hundreds
years.h: Burn practices in South Williamsburg, plays the Lower East Side
years.p: Burn rehearses in South Williamsburg and plays CBGB, the Pyramid Club and ABC No Rio, in a New York that Gavin Van Vlack remembers as wide open.
years.xp:
Van Vlack's road to Burn was rough. He told No Echo his family moved to New York from New Hampshire when his mother needed cancer treatment at Sloan Kettering; he landed in foster care, and from 15 on he slept in abandoned buildings and on friends' floors, with [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] sometimes sneaking him into his parents' house.

Before hardcore there was graffiti: he wrote NATZ with the SPORTS crew in the eighties. The son of a Mexican mother and a Dutch father, he's said both sides of the family were hostile to the mix. That street-level looseness came onto the stage with him.

years.p: Burn's four-song debut. Writer Anthony Pappalardo heard fire and fusion, pounding the pavement like demo-era [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]].
years.xp:
Chaka Malik came up with the cover concept, and Revelation's own page calls the record groundbreaking.

What set it apart was the rhythm: swing and sudden dynamic drops where other bands just went faster. Revelation's catalog lists a first run split between black and pink vinyl, and the record has been repressed ever since.

years.p: The drummer joins [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]]' new band, and Burn can't find anyone who plays at Cage's level.

eras.title: Greenpoint, and a record that waited a decade
eras.text: Without Cage the band kept writing, moved to Greenpoint, and recorded in 1992. Then it ended, and the members scattered into the noisier, heavier bands of the nineties.

years.p: Chaka Malik starts [[Orange 9mm|66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51]]. Gavin Van Vlack goes on to [[Die 116|59ff819b-b635-473d-ba52-f61d44835bd7]], Pry and The Big Collapse.

eras.title: Cleanse
eras.text: A short return in 1998 grew into a new line-up with Vic DiCara, of Inside Out and 108, on second guitar. Two releases came out of it, one brand new, one ten years old.

years.p: Burn plays again for the first time since the 1992 split.

years.h: Live at Coney Island High, NYC, December 30, 1997
yt: Live at Coney Island High, NYC, December 30, 1997

years.p: Chaka Malik and Gavin Van Vlack with Vic DiCara on second guitar and Manny Carrero, later of [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]], on bass.

years.h: Burn's Last Great Sea: the 1992 session, finally
years.p: Burn taped new songs in Greenpoint, Brooklyn in 1992, just before breaking up. Revelation released them ten years later as Last Great Sea.
years.xp: Chaka Malik has said nothing in their new Brooklyn base was established yet when they recorded.

eras.title: The word is real
eras.text: Twenty-five years after the seven-inch, Burn came back as a working band rather than a reunion act. New players, new records, and in 2017 the first full-length they'd ever made.

q: The word that comes to mind, is real.
years.src: No Echo · Black N' Blue Productions · Brooklyn Vegan
years.h: Burn plays the Black N' Blue Bowl
years.p: Burn is added as an exclusive appearance at the New York hardcore festival's May weekend, with [[Durijah Lang|42c3124a-fa12-4e3f-a373-6bc155dd416f]] on drums and Manny Carrero on bass.
years.xp: Chaka Malik said the plan was to play more in the style of the original four-song 1990 seven-inch rather than chase the later records.

years.p: A Burn show in London on October 4, then Santa Ana, Berkeley and Los Angeles from October 9 to 11.
The first new Burn music since Cleanse in 2001.

years.h: Burn's Do or Die, the band's first full-length
years.p: Released twenty-eight years after Burn started, on Deathwish Inc., produced by [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] and mastered by Howie Weinberg.
